title: Plan review — merge duplicate feedback threads

masthead.headline: Six steps, three owners, and one of them is in the wrong order.
masthead.lede: This board is laid out to be argued with. The sequence, the owner of each step, and the risk each one carries are stated separately, because a plan usually fails at a seam between two of the three.

points.text: A week of running the similarity pass in shadow, writing candidate pairs to a table nobody acts on, so the threshold is chosen from real pairs rather than from a guess.

points.lead: Merge is a link, not a deletion.
points.text: A merged thread keeps its own row and gains a pointer to the survivor. Unmerging is deleting the pointer, which is what makes the whole thing reversible.

points.lead: The irreversible step is last and separate.
points.text: Collapsing merged threads out of the index is step 6, one release after everything else, and it is the only step that cannot be undone by a flag.

items.title: 1 · Shadow the similarity pass
items.text: Run it nightly against the last 90 days of threads, writing candidate pairs to a review table. Nothing merges. One week.

items.title: 2 · Choose the threshold from the shadow output
items.text: Pick the score above which pairs are genuinely the same complaint, by reading a sample of 200 pairs rather than by tuning against a metric.

items.title: 3 · Ship the merge pointer, off by default
items.text: Schema, API and the unmerge path, all behind a flag. No thread is merged by this release.

items.title: 4 · Enable for one workspace
items.text: The internal workspace first, for two weeks, with every merge reviewable and reversible from the UI.

items.title: 5 · Enable for everyone
items.text: Flag on by default. Unmerge stays available and stays used — if nobody unmerges anything, the threshold is probably too conservative.

items.title: 6 · Collapse merged threads out of the index
items.text: The only irreversible step: merged threads stop appearing as separate rows in search. One release later, deliberately.

people.name: Search platform
people.due: Not scheduled — see the risk below

blocks.title: Step 6 has an owner who has not agreed to it
blocks.lead: Search platform was named, not asked.
blocks.text: Every other step sits with a team that has scheduled it. Step 6 is the irreversible one, it belongs to a team with its own roadmap, and the plan currently assumes their availability. That assumption is the plan's weakest joint.

rows.text: Flag off, then drop the column
Flag off; pointers remain but are ignored
Readers see threads unmerge under them
Same, at a scale people will notice
Rebuilding the index from the pointer table
Hours of reindexing, and search is degraded throughout

rows.risk: The threshold is chosen against the shadow sample and is wrong for a workspace unlike it
rows.likelihood: Moderate — the sample is one product's threads
rows.mitigation: Step 4 is a different workspace on purpose, and the threshold is per-workspace configurable before step 5.

rows.risk: Merging loses a reply that was only on the folded thread
rows.likelihood: Low if merge is a pointer
mitigation: The folded thread keeps its rows; the merge writes
and nothing else. No delete path is added in this plan at all.

rows.risk: Search platform cannot take step 6 this quarter
rows.likelihood: Likely — it is not on their roadmap
rows.mitigation: None currently. This is the open item this review is meant to settle.

rows.risk: Nobody unmerges anything and the threshold is silently too conservative
rows.mitigation: Unmerge rate is reported weekly; a rate of zero after two weeks triggers a threshold review rather than a celebration.

blocks.summary: Why step 6 exists at all, given it is the only irreversible one

blocks.text: Without it, a merged thread still appears in search as its own result, so the duplicate the reader was meant to stop seeing is still the first thing they see. Steps 1 to 5 make merging safe; step 6 is what makes it useful.

It could be made reversible by keeping the collapsed rows in a second index, at roughly the storage cost of the index itself. That has not been priced, and pricing it is a reasonable outcome of this review.

sections.title: Three things this plan needs from you.

blocks.label: Step 6 ownership
blocks.ask: Approve the plan on the condition that step 6 is not scheduled until search platform has accepted it, and steps 1–5 proceed regardless?
blocks.placeholder: If you would rather hold the whole plan until step 6 has an owner, say so.

options.summary: The single global threshold does not survive contact with a second product.

options.value: Price the reversible index before step 6
options.summary: Know what the second index costs before accepting an irreversible step.
A rate of zero is a signal, not a success.

options.value: No delete path in this plan, ever
options.summary: Merging never removes rows; a separate plan may argue for deletion.
